hero.description: Oil prices have fallen for a third consecutive session, but Brent and WTI remain above $100 as Saudi Arabia works on alternative export routes and commercial shipping through Hormuz remains far below normal.

featured.title: Hormuz Shipping Remains Far Below Normal as Oil Prices Ease
featured.content: Four commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, according to preliminary tracking data, down from six the previous day and below the 10-day average of about 16. Before the current conflict, the waterway carried roughly one-fifth of global oil and gas shipments. Oil prices have nevertheless fallen for a third consecutive session as Saudi Arabia works to restore part of its East-West pipeline and increases crude transfers through alternative routes near Oman.
featured.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz tanker vessels oil shipping

articles.title: Hormuz Records Four Commodity Vessel Crossings
articles.content: Preliminary tracking data shows four commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday. Three were entering the Gulf and one was leaving. The vessels included two Panamax tankers, one Supramax ship and one Kamsarmax vessel. The figures can change because ships sometimes switch off their tracking transponders while operating in conflict zones.

articles.title: Oil Prices Fall for a Third Consecutive Session
articles.content: Brent crude fell to around $103.77 per barrel early Friday, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate was around $100.88. Markets are responding to efforts to maintain Middle Eastern oil exports through alternative routes, although geopolitical and shipping risks remain significant.
articles.imageQuery: crude oil barrels global oil market

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Works to Restore Damaged Oil Pipeline
articles.content: Saudi Arabia is working to restore part of its East-West oil pipeline after damage disrupted crude movements towards the Red Sea. Reuters reports that three pumping stations were damaged. Riyadh is also increasing ship-to-ship crude transfers near Oman's Sohar port to help maintain supplies to Asian customers while repairs continue.
articles.imageQuery: Saudi Arabia oil pipeline crude tanker Oman Sohar

articles.title: Iran Reports Strike on Togo-Flagged Tanker in Hormuz
articles.content: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy says it struck a Togo-flagged oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, alleging that the vessel was attempting an unauthorised passage. The report comes amid continuing uncertainty over commercial shipping through the waterway. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain subject to further reporting.
articles.imageQuery: oil tanker Strait of Hormuz Gulf

articles.title: Russia Launches Fresh Wave of Strikes Across Ukraine
articles.content: Russia launched a major overnight missile and drone attack across Ukraine, with Ukrainian officials reporting more than 20 people injured. Kyiv reported 20 wounded, while Odesa recorded six injuries and Zaporizhzhia three. Eight Ukrainian regions reported damage. Energy infrastructure in Sumy and Odesa was among the sites affected.
articles.imageQuery: Kyiv Ukraine Russian missile drone attack damage

articles.title: Poland Activates Military Aviation After Strikes Near Border
articles.content: Poland temporarily activated military aircraft after Russian strikes in western Ukraine near its border. Polish authorities said there was no violation of Polish airspace, and the military operation was later completed. Airports in Rzeszow and Lublin were temporarily affected before reopening.
articles.imageQuery: Poland military jets NATO Ukraine border

articles.title: EU to Provide €3.3 Billion for Ukrainian Missiles and Drones
articles.content: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the European Union would disburse €3.3 billion to Ukraine for the procurement of missiles and drones. The announcement followed a telephone conversation with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who described discussions on strengthening Ukraine's defence resilience as productive.
articles.imageQuery: European Union Ukraine flags defence aid

articles.title: Dangote IPO Continues to Draw Heavy Retail Demand
articles.content: Nigeria's Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO continues to attract substantial interest from individual investors. Several digital investment platforms experienced technical problems when demand surged after the offer opened. Reuters reported that traffic on one major platform rose to around ten times its normal level within 30 minutes.

articles.title: Dangote IPO Offers 4.1 Billion Shares
articles.content: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery public offer consists of 4.1 billion shares priced at ₦525 each. The minimum subscription is 10 shares, while the offer is scheduled to close on 13 October 2026. Investors are being urged to use only authorised subscription channels.
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria stock market IPO Lagos investment

articles.title: SEC Warns Investors About Dangote IPO Scams
articles.content: Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission is warning prospective investors about fraudulent websites, phishing attempts and people falsely claiming to represent the Dangote IPO. Investors should independently verify receiving agents and payment instructions before transferring money or providing personal information.
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria SEC investor warning financial fraud

articles.title: Dangote Refinery Expands Nigeria's Role in Global Fuel Markets
articles.content: Dangote Refinery reported $1.82 billion in net profit during the first half of 2026, with revenue exceeding $13 billion. The refinery has also become an important supplier of jet fuel and diesel to Europe during disruptions to Middle Eastern fuel exports. Its planned expansion would increase capacity from around 700,000 barrels per day to 1.4 million barrels per day.

articles.title: Europe Discusses New Security Partnerships
articles.content: European leaders are examining stronger cooperation with countries including Canada, Britain, Norway and Ukraine as the continent responds to military, cyber and hybrid-security concerns. The European Commission has proposed a European Security Council and an emergency protocol for coordinating responses to serious crises.
articles.imageQuery: European Union security defence meeting Brussels

articles.title: EU-Canada Relationship Moves Towards Deeper Strategic Cooperation
articles.content: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed opening the way for Canada to become the EU's first associate member. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has welcomed deeper strategic cooperation covering areas such as defence, critical minerals, artificial intelligence and energy security. The proposed associate status is not the same as EU membership and its terms remain undefined.
articles.imageQuery: Canada EU flags Mark Carney Brussels

articles.title: New Zealand Says No EU Associate-Membership Talks Have Taken Place
articles.content: New Zealand's government says it has not held discussions with the European Union about becoming an associate member. The clarification follows comments that countries such as Australia and New Zealand could potentially deepen their relationships with the EU. Australia has separately expressed interest in closer ties.
articles.imageQuery: New Zealand European Union flags diplomacy

articles.title: ECB Policymaker Sees No Clear Second-Round Inflation Effect
articles.content: European Central Bank policymaker Olli Rehn said there are currently no clear signs that higher energy prices are generating a second wave of inflation through wages and broader price-setting. He said the ECB continues to monitor energy prices, labour-market conditions and other economic data.

articles.title: Bab el-Mandeb Also Remains Under Pressure
articles.content: Twenty-three commodity vessels crossed the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Thursday, below the recent 10-day average of about 26. The waterway is increasingly important as an alternative route for Gulf energy exports while Hormuz traffic remains restricted. Security risks around Yemen and the Red Sea continue to affect shipping decisions.

morningSummary: Good morning. Oil prices have fallen for a third consecutive session, but Brent and WTI remain above $100 as commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz stays severely restricted. Four commodity vessels crossed the waterway on Thursday, compared with a 10-day average of about 16. Saudi Arabia is working to restore part of its damaged East-West pipeline while using alternative crude-transfer arrangements near Oman. At the same time, Russia has launched another major attack across Ukraine, while the EU is preparing €3.3 billion for Ukrainian missile and drone procurement. In Nigeria, strong retail demand for the Dangote IPO has tested digital investment platforms, while the SEC continues to warn investors about fraud. Europe is also discussing deeper strategic partnerships with Canada and other partners, while New Zealand says it has not held associate-membership talks with the EU.
bigQuestion: If oil remains above $100 while global shipping continues to face security risks, how long can households and businesses absorb the additional costs before they become a bigger part of everyday spending?
